criteria.standardText: WCAG 2.2: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum, AA) for text, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast for UI components. The palette follows GitHub's Primer primitives, which target Level AA.
criteria.marginWhy: We hold each pair a little above the WCAG minimum. That headroom absorbs anti-aliasing, sub-pixel rendering, and future palette tweaks. It's a recommendation, not required for conformance.
criteria.enhancedWhy: Each pair is also scored against the stricter 1.4.6 Enhanced floors (body ≥ {{body}}:1, large ≥ {{large}}:1). This is reported for transparency, not required. AA is the conformance target.

form.name: Assignment name
form.slugHelp: Used in the assignment's repository names. Auto-filled from the name; edit it if you like. Must be unique in this classroom.
form.slugEditHelp: The slug is part of the assignment's repository names and can't be changed after creation.
form.setDueDateTip: Off means the assignment has no due date. Turn on to pick a date and time; students see it as the due date.
form.dueDateTz: Times are in your local timezone ({{tz}}).
form.setAvailableFromTip: Assignments are hidden from the student assignments page by default, so students can only accept via the invite link. Set a release date to list it for everyone once the date passes. Students who already accepted always see it. The release date controls listing only, not access: a private template in your organization stays readable to the classroom team. To hide a template until release, lock the assignment.
form.availableFromTz: Times are in your local timezone ({{tz}}).
form.releaseTemplateReadableTitle: Students can read this template before the release date
form.releaseTemplateReadableBody: The release date controls listing only. Saving gives the classroom team read access to this private template right away. To keep the template hidden, lock the assignment now and unlock it on the release date.
form.releaseLockedReminder: Locked. The release date doesn't unlock the assignment: turn off Lock assignment on the release date so students can accept.
form.lockAssignmentTip: Students can't see or accept a locked assignment, including students who already accepted. For a private template in your organization, the classroom team loses read access to the template until you unlock. Staff access and existing student repositories are unchanged. Use it to stage a timed assessment, then unlock when the session starts.
form.typeLockedHelp: Can't be changed after creation. Switching it would invalidate existing submissions.
form.typeTeamDisabledHelp: Group assignments need organization members to be able to create teams: the first student creates the group's team when accepting. Turn on "Allow members to create teams" in the Member team creation section of the organization settings page, or in the organization's member privileges on GitHub.
form.maxGroupSizeTitle: Must be a whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}

repoSource.label: Start with a template
repoSource.editHelp: Changing the repository source only affects repositories students accept from now on. Repositories already accepted keep their original starter content, so you'll need to update the existing repositories yourself.

none.label: No template
none.help: Create a fresh repository for each student.

template.label: Template repository
template.help: Generate each student's repository from a template you provide.

addReadme.label: Add a README
addReadme.helpOn: Start each repository with a README.md. This first commit is what lets branches, pull requests, and the Feedback PR work.
addReadme.helpOff: Start without a README. With the built-in autograder on, repositories still begin with the autograding files and grade normally. With it off, repositories are completely bare, and autograding and the Feedback PR are permanently unavailable.

includeAllBranches.label: Include all branches
includeAllBranches.help: Copy every branch and its history from the template, not just the default branch. This applies to students who accept from now on; repositories already created are not changed.

copyAbout.label: Copy About from template
copyAbout.help: Copy the template's About (its description) onto each student repository. GitHub does not copy it automatically. This applies to students who accept from now on; repositories already created are not changed.

copyTopics.label: Copy topics from template
copyTopics.help: Copy the template's topics onto each student repository. GitHub does not copy them automatically. This applies to students who accept from now on; repositories already created are not changed.

form.feedbackPrHelp: Open a pull request in each student's repository for inline review and comments on their work.
form.feedbackPrEmptyRepoHelp: Unavailable for empty repositories: there's no starter commit to compare a student's work against.

feedbackPrTemplate.label: Use the template's pull request template as the Feedback PR body
feedbackPrTemplate.help: Use the template repository's pull request template (.github/pull_request_template.md) as the body of each student's Feedback PR instead of the built-in one. You are responsible for the template's contents. If the file is missing or unreadable, the built-in body is used.
feedbackPrTemplate.checking: Checking the template for a pull request template…
feedbackPrTemplate.autoEnabled: Auto-enabled: a pull request template was found in the template repository.

studentPermission.label: Student repository access
studentPermission.help: The role each student is granted on their own assignment repository at accept time. Push (write) is the default. Choose Admin to let students manage repository settings and enable GitHub Pages. This applies to students who accept from now on; use the submissions page to change repositories already created.
studentPermission.groupHelp: Group members join with at least admin so the group owner can add teammates. This applies to repositories created from now on; use the submissions page to change existing ones.

repoVisibility.label: Repository visibility
repoVisibility.help: The visibility each student repository is created with at accept time. Private is the default. Choose Public for peer-review, portfolio, or showcase assignments. Students are warned before accepting.
repoVisibility.publicWarning: Anyone on the internet will be able to see each student's work: code, commits, and name. If the organization doesn't allow students to create public repositories, their repository is created private instead and you can make it public from the submissions page.
repoVisibility.editHelp: This applies to repositories created from now on; use the submissions page to change the visibility of existing ones.

autograding.editHelp: Changing the built-in autograder only affects repositories students accept from now on. Repositories already accepted keep their original setup, so you'll need to update the existing repositories yourself.

none.label: Do not use the built-in autograder
none.help: Grade with your own GitHub Actions workflow instead. With a template, add the workflow to it; without one, the assignment has no autograder.

built-in.label: Use the built-in autograder
built-in.help: Set up the built-in autograder, then add the tests and runtime below.

grading.label: Grading
grading.help: How this assignment is graded. "Autograded" runs the autograder you configure below. "Manual" lets you enter each student's score by hand on the submissions page. "Not graded" records no score.

maxPoints.label: Max points
maxPoints.help: Total points available for this manual assignment. Used to show each student's score out of the maximum.

submissionMode.label: Submission type
submissionMode.help: "Every push to the default branch" counts each student commit after the starter commit (the tool's own accept and autograding-update commits don't count). "A tagged commit" counts only tagged commits, so ordinary pushes use no Actions minutes; a student submits by pushing a tag or running gh student submit.
submissionMode.editWarning: Changing this only affects repositories created from now on. Repositories students already accepted keep the old setting until you update them. Use "Update autograding triggers" on the submissions page or gh teacher assignment submission-mode. Students must pull after the update.

choices.everyPush: Every push to the default branch

submissionTags.label: Submission tags
submissionTags.help: Optional tag names (one per line) whose commits also count, for example, phase1, phase2. Patterns like v* match a family of tags. Leave empty for none.
submissionTags.wildcardCaution: A broad pattern like v* matches every tag a student pushes, including unrelated release tags. Prefer exact names like phase1.
submissionTags.commaHint: Put one tag per line, not a comma-separated list. A comma becomes part of the tag name and will be rejected.

repoFeatures.heading: Repository features
repoFeatures.help: Whether each student repository has Wikis, Issues, Projects, and Pull requests enabled.
repoFeatures.helpExisting: Changes apply to repositories created from now on. To update ones students already accepted, use the submissions page.
repoFeatures.templateContentWarning: Inheriting a private template also copies its Wiki, Issues, and Projects content, so keep answer keys out of a template you inherit from.
repoFeatures.overrideTemplate: The default follows the template's settings when a student accepts. Existing repositories won't change if you update the template later.
repoFeatures.overrideNoTemplate: The default keeps GitHub's own repository defaults.
repoFeatures.overrideExisting: To update repositories students already accepted, use the bulk repository-features action on the submissions page.

form.advancedHelp: Optional grading and runtime settings. Blank fields use their documented defaults.
form.dockerImageTip: Grade inside this public Docker image instead of a GitHub-hosted runner. The image provides the OS and its packages. It must be publicly pullable (for example ubuntu:24.04).
form.containerUserTip: The user the container runs as. Set root if checkout fails with a permission error. GitHub Actions runs container steps as the host runner's user, so a non-root image often can't write to the workspace.
form.setupCommandTip: Runs once before the other tests, for example to compile or install dependencies. A non-zero exit or timeout sets the autograde status to failure without changing the numeric score; later tests still run.
form.setupTimeoutTip: New setup commands start at {{default}} seconds. Set 0 to use the runner's 10-second default, or choose a whole number from 1 through {{max}}.
form.allowedFilesTip: Ordered {{gitignore}}-style patterns, one per line, defining which files belong to a submission (last match wins, {{bang}} re-includes). For example, {{star}} then {{example}} allows only {{result}}. Blank allows every file.
form.releaseAssetsTip: One exact workspace-relative file path per line; paths are exact, not glob patterns, and may total at most 8 KiB of UTF-8 text. Files are collected after grading and attached on both passing and failing grades; missing files are skipped. Release filenames may use only ASCII letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens, and may not begin or end with a dot or contain consecutive periods.
form.passThresholdTip: Off by default. When on, the submissions page marks submissions passing or failing against the bar below (Passing rollup, score badges, passing/failing filter). This is a display threshold only. It does not change a student's actual score.

runner.label: GitHub runner
runner.tip: The GitHub Actions runner label(s) that grade this assignment. Blank uses ubuntu-latest. Combine comma-separated labels for a self-hosted runner (for example, self-hosted, linux, x64).
runner.selfHostedHint: Combine comma-separated labels for a self-hosted runner (for example, self-hosted, linux, x64).
runner.noRunnerMatch: No runner matches {{labels}}. Check the spelling.

runtime.envHostedHelp: Grades on a GitHub Actions runner.
runtime.envContainerHelp: Grades inside a public Docker image (it owns the OS packages).
runtime.languagesTip: Pick a version to install that toolchain (for example Node 26, Java 25), or type a custom one. A blank field skips it. Python defaults to 3.14 when blank on the hosted runner. You can enable as many toolchains as you need.
runtime.selfHostedDisabled: Ignored on a self-hosted runner, which uses its own prebuilt toolchains and packages. Provision these in the runner image instead.
runtime.versionTip: The {{language}} version to install (via the setup-{{language}} action). Leave blank to skip it. You can type any version the setup action accepts.
runtime.aptTip: Extra Ubuntu packages installed (apt-get) before grading, comma- or space-separated. Lowercase Debian package names.
runtime.runnerContainerError: "{{label}}" is a macOS/Windows runner; a Docker image needs an Ubuntu (or custom/self-hosted) runner.

validation.slugOverBudget: Student repositories are named "{{classroom}}-<slug>-<username>", which GitHub caps at {{limit}} characters. This slug can be at most {{budget}} characters (currently {{length}}).
validation.slugNoRoom: The classroom "{{classroom}}" leaves no room for any assignment slug: its short-name plus a username can exceed GitHub's {{limit}}-character repository-name cap. Create a classroom with a shorter slug (at most {{max}} characters) and add the assignment there.
validation.slugReserved: "{{slug}}" is the previous slug of a renamed assignment and is reserved. Reusing it would break the redirects students' renamed repositories rely on. Choose a different slug.
validation.maxGroupSizeInvalid: Max group size must be a valid number.
validation.setupTimeoutRange: Setup timeout must be 0 or a whole number of seconds from 1 through {{max}}.
validation.passThresholdRange: Pass threshold must be a whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}.
validation.studentPermissionInvalid: Student repository access must be one of pull, triage, push, maintain, or admin.
validation.gradingMaxPointsInvalid: Max points must be a whole number of at least {{min}}.
validation.releaseAssetsTooMany: Choose at most {{max}} submission release files (currently {{count}}).
validation.releaseAssetsTooLarge: Submission release file paths may total at most {{max}} UTF-8 bytes (8 KiB); currently {{bytes}}.
validation.releaseAssetsInvalidPath: {{path}} is not an exact workspace-relative file path.
validation.releaseAssetsInvalidBasename: {{basename}} is not a safe Release filename or is reserved.
validation.releaseAssetsDuplicatePath: {{path}} is listed more than once; each release file path must be unique.
validation.releaseAssetsDuplicateBasename: {{basename}} would be uploaded more than once; Release filenames must be unique.

form.teamFormationStudentHelp: The first student creates the group when accepting, then adds teammates up to the max group size.

autograder.heading: Autograding tests
autograder.empty: No autograding tests have been defined yet.
autograder.editTestHint: Pick a test type, then fill in the command and pass criteria. Commands run in the student's repository checkout.
autograder.setupCommandPlaceholder: optional, for example, gcc -o hello hello.c
autograder.runCommandHint: Runs in the student's repository checkout. Uploaded test files are under $CLASSROOM50_BUNDLE_DIR.
autograder.inputPlaceholder: optional: text fed to the command on stdin
autograder.comparisonIncluded: Included: expected appears anywhere in the output
autograder.comparisonExact: Exact: output equals expected (surrounding whitespace ignored)
autograder.exitCodeHint: Leave empty to require a successful exit (0).
autograder.pythonNote: The run command should invoke pytest (for example, python3 -m pytest -q) against test files in the assignment template. pytest and pytest-json-report are installed automatically. Points are split across the cases pytest discovers.
autograder.failureDetailsHint: How much of a failing run students see in the submission report and workflow log.
autograder.failureDetailsFull: Full: diff or expected and actual output
autograder.failureDetailsActualOnly: Student output only (never the expected output)
autograder.showOutputHint: Include the captured setup/run output in the report even when the test passes, inside a collapsed section.
autograder.reportOptionsHint: What the submission report shows for this test. Both options start at the assignment's report defaults; pick another value to override it for this test only.

defaults.heading: Report defaults
defaults.hint: Defaults for every test; a test's own report options override them.
defaults.failureDetailsFull: Full: diff or expected and actual output
defaults.showOutputHelp: Adds each passing test's captured setup/run output to the submission report and workflow log, collapsed by default. Useful when authoring or debugging an autograder.

teacherFiles.title: Upload teacher-only test files
teacherFiles.subtitle: Students get every file in the template. Keep test scripts and fixtures they must not see in the classroom50 repository instead.
teacherFiles.howTo: Click Open upload page, drop your files in, and commit. They go to {{path}}; GitHub creates the folder if needed. Publishing takes a few minutes after the commit.
teacherFiles.usage: Test commands find the folder at $CLASSROOM50_BUNDLE_DIR. For example, a Run command test that calls an uploaded check.sh:
teacherFiles.note: Don't upload a file named autograder.py: it replaces the tests on this page.
teacherFiles.readableTitle: Students can't change these files, but they can read them
teacherFiles.readableBody: They're published on your organization's public GitHub Pages site. Keep full solutions and private data out, and use Failure details shown to students to hide expected output.
teacherFiles.unsaved: Create the assignment first. Test files go in a folder named after the assignment, so this guide opens once it exists.

io.label: Input/Output
io.hint: Run a command, feed it stdin, and compare its stdout against an expected value.

run.label: Run command
run.hint: Run a command and pass when its exit code matches (0 by default).

python.label: Python (pytest)
python.hint: Run a pytest command; points are split across discovered test cases at grade time.

template.help: Optional. Students receive a copy of this repository. Search your organization's template repositories, or type <owner>/<repo> or paste a GitHub URL to use one from anywhere. search.noTemplates: No template repositories found in this organization. Turn on "Template repository" in a repo's settings, or paste a GitHub URL.

template.privateWillGrant: Private template in {{owner}} (branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>). The classroom team doesn't have access yet; it'll be added automatically when you create the assignment, so students can copy it.
template.okPublic: Public template in {{owner}}, branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>. Students can access it.
template.okPrivate: Private template in {{owner}}, branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>. Students can access it.
template.okPublicInOrg: Public template, branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>. Students can access it.
template.okPrivateInOrg: Private template, branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>. Students can access it.
template.nonMainBranch: This template's default branch is <branch>{{branch}}</branch>, not "main". The assignment will use it, and student autograding keys off that branch.
template.branchIgnored: A custom branch (<branch>{{branch}}</branch>) was specified and will be ignored: the assignment copies the template's default branch. To use a different branch, change the template repository's default branch.
template.okVerify: Reachable in {{owner}} (branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>). If {{owner}} restricts third-party apps, students can't copy it until an owner approves Classroom 50.
template.notVisible: {{owner}}/{{repo}} isn't visible to you. Make it public or copy it into {{org}}.
template.notTemplate: {{owner}}/{{repo}} isn't a template repository. Enable that in the repository's Settings on GitHub.
template.emptyTemplate: {{owner}}/{{repo}} is a template but has no commits. Add at least one commit (for example, a README), then retry.
template.restricted: {{owner}} blocked access to {{repo}} (HTTP 403), likely a third-party app restriction. Try, in order:
template.restrictedItemApprove: Approve Classroom 50 for {{owner}} (Org settings → Third-party access).
template.restrictedItemFork: If {{repo}} is a fork, approve Classroom 50 on the fork's upstream organization too. A private fork's access follows the upstream organization's policy.
template.restrictedItemOther: Otherwise it may be a different 403; see GitHub's message below.
template.restrictedScope: {{owner}} blocked access to {{repo}} (HTTP 403). GitHub says your token is missing a required scope. Sign out and back in to refresh your GitHub authorization, then retry.
template.privateForkCrossOrg: {{owner}}/{{repo}} is a private fork of {{parent}} (branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>). <important>Important: {{parentOrg}} must keep Classroom 50 approved. If that approval is ever removed, students will fail to accept (HTTP 403).</important> To avoid depending on {{parentOrg}}, use a fresh non-fork repository: create a new repository and copy the fork's contents into it.
template.privateForkInOrg: {{owner}}/{{repo}} is a private fork of {{parent}} (branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>). The upstream is in this organization, so copying should work, but a fresh non-fork template repository is more predictable if accept fails.
template.privateForkNoParent: {{owner}}/{{repo}} is a private fork (branch <branch>{{branch}}</branch>). <important>Important: the fork's upstream organization must keep Classroom 50 approved. rename.sectionBody: The slug <slug>{{slug}}</slug> is too long. Repository names built from it can exceed GitHub's {{limit}}-character limit, so some students cannot accept this assignment. Updating the slug renames every student repository to match, and GitHub redirects the old names so existing clones keep working.
rename.sectionFinishBody: The slug changed from <from>{{from}}</from>, but some student repositories still use the old name. The assignment stays locked until every repository is renamed.
rename.title: Update assignment slug
rename.subtitle: One-time update of <old>{{old}}</old> that renames every existing student repository.
rename.finishSubtitle: Renames the student repositories left over from updating <old>{{old}}</old> to <new>{{new}}</new>.
rename.enterNewName: Enter a new slug to rename the assignment.
rename.budgetHint: At most {{budget}} characters in this classroom (currently {{length}}).
rename.repoCount_one: {{count}} existing student repository will be renamed.
rename.repoCount_other: {{count}} existing student repositories will be renamed.
rename.warning: You can update a slug only once: the old slug stays reserved so GitHub can redirect student clones to the renamed repositories. The assignment stays locked while repositories are renamed. Students need to run "git pull" once before their next submit.
rename.failedSection: Failed ({{count}}): fix the causes and finish the rename. It's safe to run again.
rename.lockNote: "{{slug}}" stays locked while repositories are unrenamed: an accept now would occupy a pending repository name and strand that student's work. Finish the rename to release it.
rename.lockRestoreFailed: Every repository landed, but releasing the assignment lock failed. Unlock it from the assignments list.
rename.resumeUnlockNote: All repositories are healed. If the original rename locked "{{slug}}", unlock it from the assignments list.

error.sameSlug: The new slug is the same as the current one, so there's nothing to rename.
error.overBudget: "{{slug}}" still exceeds the repository-name budget for classroom "{{classroom}}".
error.alreadyRenamed: This assignment was already renamed once (from "{{from}}"). A rename is one-shot, so it can't be renamed again.

validate.scopeHint: Create a fine-grained personal access token with Resource owner set to {{org}} and Repository access set to All repositories. Under Repository permissions, set Contents, Actions, and Administration to Read and write: collecting scores reads student repositories and grants staff teams access to them, and regrading re-runs autograde workflows and may push submit tags. Under Organization permissions, set Members to Read: collection lists the classroom team, which no repository permission covers. If your organization requires token approval and you are not an owner, an owner must approve the token first.
validate.invalid: This token is invalid, expired, or revoked. Create a new fine-grained token and try again.
validate.configRepoMissing: Couldn't find a {{repo}} repository in {{org}}. Check that the organization is correct and that setup has been run for it. This isn't necessarily a problem with the token.
validate.unreachable: Couldn't reach GitHub to verify the token. Check your connection and try again. ({{reason}})
validate.readOnly: This token can read {{org}}/{{repo}} but can't write to it. Collecting scores needs read access, and regrading needs write access. {{hint}}
validate.noAdmin: This token can read and write {{org}}/{{repo}} but can't administer it. Collecting scores grants staff teams, such as TAs, read access to student repositories, which needs Administration set to Read and write. {{hint}}
validate.noMembersRead: This token can read {{org}}/{{repo}} but can't read the organization's members. Collecting scores lists the classroom team, which needs Members set to Read under Organization permissions. {{hint}}
validate.selectedRepos: This token can read {{org}}/{{repo}} but not {{org}}/{{probe}}, so its Repository access is limited to selected repositories, or its Resource owner isn't {{org}}. Collecting scores reads every student repository and grants staff teams access to them. Create the token again with Resource owner set to {{org}} and Repository access set to All repositories, keeping the same permissions.

orgDefaults.title: Organization safety defaults
orgDefaults.what: Locks down organization member privileges to safe defaults (base permissions, repo creation, visibility changes, and related settings).
orgDefaults.why: Stops students from changing or deleting each other's repositories, or making private classroom work public.
orgDefaults.remediation: Open the organization member-privileges page and apply the flagged settings by hand. Some are controlled by an enterprise policy and can only be set there.

orgActions.title: Actions permissions
orgActions.what: Enables GitHub Actions for the organization.
orgActions.why: Autograding and the published assignment site run as Actions workflows, so they can't run until Actions is enabled.
orgActions.remediation: Open the organization Actions settings and allow Actions to run (set the policy to allow all actions, or at minimum the workflows Classroom 50 ships).

orgBudget.title: Actions spending cap
orgBudget.what: Creates a $0 GitHub Actions spending cap (only if none exists).
orgBudget.why: A $0 hard-stop budget blocks paid Actions minutes, so a runaway autograde workflow can't run up a bill. An existing budget you set is left untouched.
orgBudget.remediation: Open the organization billing budgets settings and set a $0 GitHub Actions budget with "prevent further usage" enabled (needs Organization Administration access).

orgPrCreation.title: Actions pull request creation
orgPrCreation.what: Allows GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests in the organization.
orgPrCreation.why: Some Classroom 50 workflows open pull requests on a student's behalf; without this they fail with a permissions error.
orgPrCreation.remediation: Open the organization Actions settings and enable "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests".

configRepo.title: classroom50 repository
configRepo.what: Creates the private classroom50 repository in the organization.
configRepo.why: Classroom 50 has no backend: this repository holds all classroom config, manifests, workflows, and scores.
configRepo.remediation: This is a required step. Re-run setup; if it keeps failing, confirm you have owner permissions and that an organization or enterprise policy isn't blocking private repository creation.

skeleton.title: Workflow files
skeleton.what: Commits or updates the workflow and script files Classroom 50 needs in the classroom50 repository.
skeleton.why: These bundled files run autograding, publishing, and scoring; re-running setup also upgrades them to the latest version.
skeleton.remediation: This is a required step. Re-run setup; if it keeps failing, check that you can push to the classroom50 repository's default branch.

branchProtection.title: Branch protection
branchProtection.what: Protects the classroom50 repository's main branch.
branchProtection.why: Keeps the source-of-truth config and scores from being force-pushed or deleted.
branchProtection.remediation: Open the repository branch settings and protect the main branch, or re-run setup to re-apply it.

workflowPermissions.title: Workflow permissions
workflowPermissions.what: Sets the default GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permissions for the classroom50 repository.
workflowPermissions.why: Autograding and publishing workflows need write access to commit results and deploy Pages.
workflowPermissions.remediation: Open the repository Actions settings and set workflow permissions to read and write, or re-run setup.

reusableWorkflowAccess.title: Reusable workflow access
reusableWorkflowAccess.what: Allows other repositories in the organization to use the reusable workflows in classroom50.
reusableWorkflowAccess.why: Assignment repositories call the shared autograding workflow from classroom50; without access sharing, their runs fail.
reusableWorkflowAccess.remediation: Open the repository Actions settings and, under "Access", allow access from repositories in the organization. Or re-run setup.

pages.title: GitHub Pages
pages.what: Enables GitHub Pages for the classroom50 repository (built from Actions).
pages.why: Published assignment instructions and dashboards are served from this Pages site.
pages.remediation: Open the repository Pages settings and enable Pages with the GitHub Actions source. Pages from a private repository may require GitHub Team or Enterprise.

rulesets.title: Branch protection rulesets
rulesets.what: Creates organization rulesets that protect classroom and assignment repositories.
rulesets.why: Rulesets enforce the classroom guardrails (protected branches, restricted deletions) across every repository the organization creates.
rulesets.remediation: Open the organization rulesets page to review them, or re-run setup to re-apply. Rulesets may require GitHub Team or Enterprise.
